subject: Re: [knitr] Changing plot size in knitr/spin

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Changing plot size in knitr/spin
parts:
For fig.height/fig.width, you can only have one set of values for one
chunk. For out.width/out.height, you can vectorize them, e.g.
out.width=c('500px', '200px') for two plots.

If you want different fig.width/fig.height for plots, you have to put
them in different chunks.

On Wed, Dec 19, 2012 at 7:45 AM, <dieter...@menne-biomed.de> wrote:
>
> I know that I cannot create different figure sizes in one chunk, but what
> should I do to have different sizes for the splom and xyplot in the example
> below?
>
>
> #' Knitr/spin in functions
> #' =======================
> #+ include=FALSE, echo=FALSE
> #' spin in functions: Different plot sizes
> library(lattice)
> library(knitr)
> opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE,comment=NA)
> data(iris)
>
> # Minor problem, probably a feature: Note that this one has comment ="##"
> table(iris$Species)
>
> #' opt_chunks are only active after some text
> table(iris$Species)
> # Chunk name and fig.height(small) are accepted
> #+ splom,fig.height=4
> splom(iris, main="Size 4 called from global")
>
> #' Called from a function
> mySplom = function(){
> # I want this one very big
> opts_chunk$set(fig.height=20)
> p = splom(iris, main="Called from function")
> # MUST use print(p) here.
> print(p)
> # I want this one small
> opts_chunk$set(fig.height=4)
> p = xyplot(Sepal.Width~Sepal.Length,data=iris)
> print(p)
> return (NULL)
> }
>
> mySplom()
